method: Per terrace, the representative photo (survey crop, camera centred on the rep house) was cropped to three house widths with the rep footprint (green) and its centre (pink) drawn; the rep house handedness is read from the door against the centre line and the order small window / door / big window, the neighbours decide alternating pairs against a uniform row. Normal = big window left of the door, small window right (the spec order); mirrored = the reverse.
findings: The earlier start parity (leftmost house normal, then alternating) matched ~25 % of 40 read terraces; leftmost house mirrored matched ~80 % of the even-sized ones, odd-sized terraces split, so the start parity is pinned per terrace here. The Geuzenveld porch group (terraces 233-282) is a uniform row, not alternating pairs. The render-tile design (D) is uniform in all 81 terraces.

door-window.default: unread (flip close-ups, dark or hidden photos, the 305+ porch pairs): leftmost house of the terrace mirrored, then alternating

garage-door: uniform, not mirrored (6 terraces checked on camera sheets)
